title: A Door Made of Paper: Why Reading Brings Real Joy
title_zh: 一扇纸做的门：阅读为何带来真正的快乐
intro_zh: 本文约522词，围绕阅读带来的真实快乐展开，适合CET-4水平阅读训练，包含科普数据、生活场景与细节理解题。

paragraphs.en: On a rainy Friday evening, two people sit in the same room. One scrolls through short videos; the other opens a paperback. After an hour, the first person feels tired but cannot say why. The second looks up, smiles, and says, 'I have just been to a village in Japan.' Nothing magical has happened. A page has simply done its quiet work. Why does reading, an activity that looks so still, make us feel so alive?
paragraphs.zh: 一个下雨的周五晚上，两个人坐在同一个房间里。一个人刷着短视频；另一个人翻开一本平装书。一小时后，第一个人觉得累，却说不出为什么。第二个人抬起头，笑了笑，说：“我刚去了一趟日本的一个村庄。”并没有什么神奇的事发生。只是一页纸静静地完成了它的工作。阅读看起来如此安静，为什么却让我们觉得如此有生气？

paragraphs.en: Scientists have a clue. When we read a story, the brain does not treat words as dead marks. In one study, people read about a character walking through a forest. Brain areas linked to smell and movement became active, as if the readers were there. We build the scene with our own memories: the smell of rain, the sound of a door. This is why two readers can enjoy the same book in different ways.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家找到了一条线索。当我们读故事时，大脑并不把文字当作死板的符号。在一项研究中，人们读到一个人物穿过森林。与嗅觉和运动有关的大脑区域变得活跃，仿佛读者就在那里。我们用自己的记忆搭建场景：雨的气味、门的声音。这就是为什么两个读者能以不同方式享受同一本书。

paragraphs.en: Stories also let us try other lives safely. A novel can put us inside a person we might never meet. This exercise in fiction seems to strengthen empathy, our ability to feel with others. Researchers have found that readers of literary stories often score higher on tests of understanding emotions. The pleasure is not only escape. It is the warm surprise of caring about someone who does not exist.
paragraphs.zh: 故事还让我们安全地体验另一种人生。一部小说能把我们放进一个也许永远不会遇见的人的身体里。这种虚构作品的练习似乎能增强共情，也就是我们与他人感同身受的能力。研究者发现，文学故事的读者在理解情绪的测试中往往得分更高。这种快乐不只是逃避。它是一种温暖的惊喜：我们会关心一个并不存在的人。

paragraphs.en: Reading can also calm the body. A well-known study at the University of Sussex asked people to try different ways to relax. Reading for just six minutes reduced stress by 68%, more than listening to music or taking a walk. The reason is simple: a good page gives the mind one clear place to rest. Worries about work and money lose their hold, at least for a while.
paragraphs.zh: 阅读还能让身体平静下来。苏塞克斯大学一项著名研究请人们尝试不同的放松方式。仅仅阅读六分钟，压力就降低了68%，比听音乐或散步的效果更好。原因很简单：好的一页给大脑一个清晰的休息之处。对工作和金钱的担忧会暂时失去控制力，至少在一段时间内如此。

paragraphs.en: In a day full of messages, reading offers a rare kind of escape. It is not running away from life, but stepping into a smaller, cleaner room for a moment. You cannot check a novel every three seconds and still follow its story. You must concentrate, and that effort feels surprisingly good. The mind stops jumping and begins to move in a straight line.
paragraphs.zh: 在充满信息的一天里，阅读提供了一种难得的逃离。它不是逃离生活，而是暂时走进一个更小、更干净的房间。你不可能每三秒看一次手机，还仍然跟得上一部小说的故事。你必须专注，而这种努力出奇地令人愉快。大脑停止跳跃，开始沿直线前进。

paragraphs.en: Some people think reading is lonely. In fact, it often connects us. A book passed between friends carries marks and notes. A reading group turns private pages into shared questions. Even reading alone can create a silent conversation with an author who lived a hundred years ago. We absorb not only facts but also a voice, a way of seeing.
paragraphs.zh: 有些人认为阅读是孤独的。事实上，它常常把我们连接起来。朋友之间传递的一本书带着标记和笔记。读书小组把私人的书页变成共同的问题。即使独自阅读，也能与一位生活在百年前的作者进行无声的对话。我们不仅吸收事实，还吸收一种声音、一种看世界的方式。

paragraphs.en: The reward of reading is not a finished list or a gold star. It arrives in small moments: a sentence you underline, a character you miss, a fact you repeat at dinner. You may forget most of a book, yet a few lines stay. They become part of how you think and speak.
paragraphs.zh: 阅读的回报不是一份完成的清单或一颗金星。它出现在小小的瞬间里：你划下的一句话、一个你惦记的人物、一个你在晚餐时重复的事实。你可能忘掉一本书的大部分内容，但有几行会留下来。它们成为你思考和说话方式的一部分。

paragraphs.en: So the next time you feel tired of screens, pick up something short. Read for six minutes. You may not finish a chapter or learn a lesson. But you may look up and feel that the room is a little larger, and that you are a little less alone. That is the quiet joy of a paper door.
paragraphs.zh: 所以，下次你厌倦屏幕时，拿起一本短小的书。读上六分钟。你也许没有读完一章，也没有学到什么道理。但你抬起头时，可能会觉得房间变大了一点，而你也少了一点孤独。这就是一扇纸门带来的安静快乐。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Reading is mainly a way to finish more books quickly.
Reading brings joy by calming the mind and letting us enter other lives.
Reading is useful only for passing language exams.
Reading is less relaxing than watching short videos.
questions.explain: 文章从大脑模拟、共情、减压、专注和人际连接等角度说明阅读带来的快乐，中心是阅读既能平静心灵，又能让人体验他人生活。

questions.q: According to the University of Sussex study, what happened when people read for six minutes?
questions.explain: 第四段明确提到，苏塞克斯大学的研究发现阅读六分钟使压力降低68%，效果超过听音乐或散步。

questions.q: What can we infer about reading from paragraph 5?
options: It requires some attention, and that effort can feel pleasant.
It is a way to avoid all real-life problems forever.
It is impossible if a phone is in the same room.
It should be done only in the morning.
questions.explain: 第五段说读小说不能每三秒看一次手机，必须专注，而这种努力出奇地令人愉快，可推断阅读需要一定注意力且这种投入带来愉悦。

questions.q: The word "absorb" in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to ___.
questions.explain: absorb在句中表示“吸收、理解”，与take in意思最接近；give up放弃，write down写下，run after追赶，均不符合语境。
